blocks.text: A **keyboard shortcut** runs a command quickly using one key or a combination of keys. In a combination the **+** sign means the keys are pressed together. **Ctrl** is short for **Control**. What a shortcut does depends on the program that is active, so always ask: which application am I in?

blocks.title: Types of keys
rows: Change the action of another key when held down with it: **Ctrl**, **Alt** and **Shift**.
Switch a mode on or off each time they are pressed: **Caps Lock**, **Num Lock** and **Scroll Lock**.
Switches the behaviour of the numeric keypad (numbers or navigation).
Changes how scrolling works in programs that support it.
**F1 to F12** along the top row; what each does depends on the program.

blocks.title: Modifier vs toggle
blocks.text: A **modifier** combines with another key (Ctrl, Alt, Shift). A **toggle** changes a mode and stays in that mode until pressed again (Caps Lock, Num Lock, Scroll Lock).

sections.title: Ctrl Commands A to M (MS Word)

blocks.title: Ctrl + letter in Microsoft Word
rows: Select all content of the document
Open Go To (page or other location)

blocks.title: Easy picks
blocks.text: Many letters are first letters: **B**old, **I**talics, **F**ind, **L**eft, **J**ustify, **P**rint. Ctrl + E centres the paragraph (cEntre), and Ctrl + H opens Find and Replace. Ctrl + D is the odd one: in Word it opens the **Font** dialog, but in a browser it bookmarks the page.

sections.title: Ctrl Commands N to Z (MS Word)

blocks.title: Ctrl + letter in Microsoft Word
rows: Redo an undone action, or repeat a supported command

blocks.title: Edit-menu favourites
blocks.text: **X** = Cut, **C** = Copy, **V** = Paste, **Z** = Undo, **Y** = Redo, **S** = Save.

blocks.title: Exam clarifications
blocks.text: Ctrl + N creates a new **document**, not a new page. Ctrl + Q resets **paragraph** formatting, not all character formatting. Ctrl + T means a **hanging indent** in Word but opens a **new tab** in a browser.

blocks.title: Memory trick
blocks.text: The X looks like a pair of scissors (Cut). Z and Y are the last two letters, and they sit side by side: Z undoes, Y redoes.

rows: Opens the Windows security screen (options include Lock, Switch user, Sign out and Task Manager)

blocks.text: Ctrl + Alt + Delete is sometimes nicknamed the **three-finger salute**. Reboot and restart both simply mean starting the computer again. On modern Windows, Ctrl + Alt + Delete does not restart the computer directly; it opens a menu from which you can choose what to do.

blocks.title: Not a direct restart
blocks.text: Old books call Ctrl + Alt + Delete the restart shortcut. On modern Windows it opens the **security screen**; Task Manager can be reached either from it or directly with **Ctrl + Shift + Esc**.

blocks.title: Quick revision keys
blocks.text: **F2** = Rename, **F7** = Proofing (spelling and grammar), **F11** = Browser full screen. **F9** updates fields in Word, not the whole document.

Close the active window; with the desktop active, it opens the shutdown dialog

blocks.text: On older Windows systems, pressing **F8** during startup opened the advanced boot options, from where Safe Mode could be chosen. Modern Windows does not rely on F8 in the same way.

blocks.title: Old versus new
blocks.text: 'F8 for Safe Mode' was true for older Windows versions. On modern Windows go through Recovery > Troubleshoot > Advanced options > Startup Settings > Restart, then press **4 or F4** for Safe Mode.

blocks.title: Window and file shortcuts

Select the Home tab in Word and supported Office programs

blocks.title: Normal reload vs hard reload
rows: Reloads the page; the browser may reuse or revalidate cached resources
Ctrl + F5 or Ctrl + Shift + R
Reloads while bypassing cached content; useful when a page shows an older version

blocks.title: Cache and hard reload
blocks.text: **Cache** is locally stored data that helps pages load faster. A hard reload skips the cache but does **not** erase all cookies, browsing history or other stored browser data.
These entries describe Chrome on Windows unless stated otherwise.

Select the tab at that position
Select the last tab, even if it is not the ninth
Move the current tab left in Chrome
Move the current tab right in Chrome

Go to the bottom of the page (when page content has focus)

blocks.text: Inside a text field, Home and End usually move to the start or end of the current line instead of the page.

blocks.title: Address bar and search
rows: Start a search through the address/search bar
In Chrome's address bar, add www. and .com around the site name and open it
Move to the next Find match in Chrome

blocks.title: Quick revision
blocks.text: Ctrl + T = new **tab**; Ctrl + N = new **window**; Ctrl + 9 = **last** tab; Esc = **stop** loading.

sections.title: Browser Tools: Zoom, Bookmarks & Page Tools

blocks.title: Bookmarks and records
rows: Show or hide the bookmarks bar
Open Clear Browsing Data; choose items and confirm the deletion

blocks.title: Page tools
rows: Find text on the current page

blocks.title: Source vs Developer Tools
blocks.text: **Page source** shows the underlying HTML. **Developer Tools** help you inspect and debug a webpage.

blocks.title: Read the application first
blocks.text: The same combination can mean different things in different programs. Before choosing an answer, identify the **application** the question is about.

blocks.title: Paste vs clipboard history
blocks.text: **Ctrl + V** pastes the current clipboard content. **Win + V** opens clipboard history so you can pick an earlier copied item.
**Win** means the key carrying the Windows logo. Hold Win while pressing the other key or keys.

Restore windows minimised with Win + M

blocks.title: Quick revision
blocks.text: Win + **D** = Desktop, Win + **E** = Explorer, Win + **L** = Lock. Win + D toggles the desktop view; Win + M only minimises windows.

revision: Modifier keys (Ctrl, Alt, Shift) combine with another key; toggle keys (Caps Lock, Num Lock, Scroll Lock) switch a mode.
Ctrl + X = Cut, C = Copy, V = Paste, Z = Undo, Y = Redo, S = Save.
Ctrl + N creates a new document (not a new page); Ctrl + Q resets paragraph formatting only.
Ctrl + T is a hanging indent in Word but a new tab in a browser.
Ctrl + Alt + Delete opens the Windows security screen; Ctrl + Shift + Esc opens Task Manager directly.
F2 = Rename, F5 = Refresh, F7 = Spelling and grammar, F11 = Browser full screen, F12 = Save As in Word.
F9 updates fields in Word; F8 opened boot options on older Windows (modern Safe Mode: Startup Settings, then 4 or F4).
Alt + Tab switches windows; Alt + F4 closes the active window; Alt + Print Screen captures the active window.
F5 or Ctrl + R is a normal reload; Ctrl + F5 or Ctrl + Shift + R is a hard reload that bypasses cache.
Browser: Ctrl + T new tab, Ctrl + W close tab, Ctrl + Shift + T reopen tab, Ctrl + N new window, Ctrl + Shift + N Incognito.
Ctrl + 9 selects the last tab; Esc stops page loading; Ctrl + 0 restores default zoom.
Ctrl + D bookmark, Ctrl + H history, Ctrl + J downloads, Ctrl + U page source, Ctrl + Shift + I or F12 Developer Tools.
Win + D desktop, Win + E File Explorer, Win + L lock, Win + I Settings, Win + S Search, Win + P projection.
Win + V opens clipboard history; Ctrl + V simply pastes. Win + M minimises all, Win + Shift + M restores them.
